        "description": "Run multiple commands in ONE call. Every command's output is auto-indexed into the knowledge base; if you also pass `queries`, the matching sections come back in the same round trip so a follow-up search call is not needed.

Concurrency parallelizes the FETCH phase (run-the-commands). Use 4-8 for I/O-bound batches; keep at 1 for CPU work or shared-state commands; lower the value when target hosts enforce per-IP rate limits.

Think-in-Code — the core philosophy: the bytes your code processes never enter your conversation memory; only what you console.log() does. Reading a 700 KB log directly means 700 KB of your remaining reasoning capacity gets spent on raw bytes. Running code over that same log in this sandbox and printing a 3 KB summary leaves you with 697 KB of capacity for the actual work.

Concrete shape — analyze 47 source files without reading any of them:
  ctx_execute(language: "javascript", code: `
    const fs = require('fs');
    const files = fs.readdirSync('src').filter(f => f.endsWith('.ts'));
    files.forEach(f => {
      const lines = fs.readFileSync('src/'+f,'utf8').split('\\n').length;
      console.log(f + ': ' + lines + ' lines');
    });
  `)

        "description": "Search a unified knowledge base with a multi-strategy ranking pipeline. Two parallel matchers run on every query: a Porter-stemming matcher ("caching" finds "cached", "caches", "cach") and a trigram-substring matcher ("useEff" finds "useEffect"). Their ranked lists are merged via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, so a document that ranks well in both surfaces above one that wins only on a single strategy. Multi-term queries get an additional proximity-rerank pass that boosts passages where the query terms appear close together. Typos are corrected via Levenshtein distance and re-searched. Result snippets are window-extracted around the matched terms, not blindly truncated.

The knowledge base is unified: queries reach indexed content you stored (ctx_index, ctx_fetch_and_index, ctx_batch_execute output) AND auto-captured session memory written by hooks (decisions, errors, blockers, plans, user prompts, rejected approaches, tool failures, compaction guides — 26 event categories). File-backed sources carry a content hash and auto-flag staleness when the source file changes.

WHEN:
  - You want to recall something that exists in storage (recently indexed content, prior session events, auto-memory) instead of re-reading raw sources
  - You have multiple related questions about the same body of knowledge — batch every question into one call (the ranking pipeline runs per-query but the round-trip cost is paid once)
  - You want to scope the query to one labelled source (pass `source` — partial match is fine)
  - You want a chronological view across current session + prior sessions + persistent auto-memory (pass `sort: "timeline"` — the default `relevance` mode only ranks within the current session)

22: pas du nom du profil. Le lead seul délègue, arbitre, intègre et valide.

25: réellement indépendantes ; alimenter les tâches prêtes sans sauter leurs
26: dépendances. Le modèle conversationnel du parent n'est pas changé par le routage

29: ## 2. Routage : catalogue dynamique et signal Jev

32: les références exactes `provider/model`, variantes et capacités disponibles.
33: L'inscription au catalogue ne prouve ni authentification, ni quota, ni coût nul.
34: Les familles ci-dessous sont des préférences utilisateur, pas une allowlist
35: figée ni un ordre de fallback permanent :
36: 
37: - Sémantique/review/réconciliation : GPT-6.1 Sol, medium/high ; xhigh pour les
38:   fonctions difficiles ou défauts nécessitant une escalade motivée.
39: - Décompilation : GPT-6 Luna (OpenCode ou OpenAI), GLM Flash, Muse Spark

42:   low/high/max. Ne pas inventer une variante ou assimiler max à xhigh.

44:   Ne pas attribuer GLM à OpenAI par analogie avec Luna. Go n'est pas une preuve
45:   d'accès à Zen et n'est pas activé par ce guide.
46: - Un nouveau modèle est un candidat à évaluer, pas automatiquement un modèle
47:   équivalent ni une permission de payer. Si coût/accès sont inconnus, bloquer
48:   cette route jusqu'à décision ou choisir une alternative déjà autorisée.

51: architecture et métadonnées extractibles à l'usage. Le mode/context versionné

71: ## 3. Pipeline et contrats aveugles
72: 
73: Futur RE : **2+1 par défaut**, séparément pour C et sémantique lorsque les deux
74: sont demandés. Deux auteurs produisent A/B indépendamment, puis R tranche
75: contre l'ASM. Diversifier les modèles de C si les capacités et le budget le
76: permettent ; deux sessions du même modèle restent indépendantes mais ne prouvent
77: pas une diversité de raisonnement. Pour la sémantique, deux sessions Sol sont
78: compatibles avec la préférence utilisateur.
79: 
80: Une variante 1+V ou 1+P doit être explicitement autorisée dans le contrat de la
81: future mission et conserver ses critères/gates. V voit A volontairement et
82: n'est donc pas B aveugle. Les modes et triggers du
83: [protocole historique](investigation/battle-static-discovery/HANDOFF_semantic-triple-review.md)
84: restent applicables à la campagne historique, sans changement par ce setup.
85: 
86: ### Entrée commune et projections
87: 
88: 1. Le superviseur produit un gel natif : bytes/ASM, frontières/chunks, CFG,
89:    xrefs code/data et contexte autorisé. Hash, version et provenance enregistrés.
90:    Il fournit le C existant seulement à un rôle autorisé à le voir.
91: 2. A et B partent en **fresh** distincts, sans fork/checkpoint/handoff du lead
92:    ou de l'autre auteur. Ne pas coller l'historique du superviseur dans le prompt.
93:    Même niveau de contexte et hash commun ; noms sémantiques dérivés exclus en
94:    mode aveugle. Le score/groupe Jev ne sert pas d'amorce aux auteurs.
95: 3. Chaque worker reçoit une projection bornée dans `inputs/` de son worktree,
96:    et écrit dans `outputs/`. Le lead fournit les fichiers explicitement : les
97:    gels ignorés/hors git ne sont pas transférés implicitement par un worktree.

100:    V reçoit uniquement le jeu nécessaire à sa review. Les lectures des sorties
101:    du voisin, du ledger cible ou d'un index contenant les résultats restent
102:    interdites pour A/B, même si le fichier existe ailleurs.
103: 5. Un slot libéré est réutilisable ; le contexte d'un auteur aveugle ne l'est
104:    pas pour un autre rôle. Repli : nouvelle session possédée, même entrée gelée,
105:    tentative précédente conservée et motif explicite.

107: Les profils dédiés sont `mode: primary` (sessions/teammates) ; les workers natifs
108: existants restent inchangés. Leurs permissions partent de deny, autorisent la
109: lecture de `inputs/`, de leurs `outputs/`, des instructions communes et l'écriture

117: ### Livrables et validation
118: 
119: - C : code complet, couverture des blocs/chunks, types/largeurs, wrap/shift,

130:   commit applicables ; ce guide n'autorise aucun commit automatique du setup.

132: ## 4. Disponibilité, concurrence et budget
133: 
134: Concurrence/budgets par **service, compte et quota réellement partagés** ; deux
135: alias fournisseur ne prouvent pas deux capacités indépendantes. Séparer tâches
136: prêtes, sessions actives utiles, sessions terminées et tentatives échouées.

138: 
139: - Auth/403/permission : désactiver la route et demander correction ; pas de retry
140:   illimité ni déduction « saturation » à partir du code seul.
141: - Entrée/schéma/context trop grand : corriger ou borner l'entrée ; versionner la

154: mesuré le maximum global de parallélisme. Reprise/cooldown événementiels bornés,
155: pas d'attente occupée ni de boucle de polling. Aucune action power/veille.

160: inputs, prédiction Jev brute et modèle, choix modèle/variante motivé et readback,
161: timestamps, tentatives et erreurs typées, hashes des sorties, review, corrections,

170: d'observation, ne pas laisser la prédiction modifier le protocole évalué : le
171: routage Jev adaptatif et la validation shadow sont deux modes distincts.

173: utilisé, pas au seul verdict CERTAIN ou au nombre d'instructions. Conserver un
174: baseline structurel ; rien n'autorise ici des seuils automatiques non évalués.

186: dépendances et outputs. Une session de capture/injection/debugger possède un
187: bail exclusif du processus et des écritures IDA. Les quatre profils RE dédiés

# Skill: opencode-ensemble

# OpenCode Ensemble

Use Ensemble to coordinate bounded, verifiable missions. The lead chooses the team shape for the actual task and owns integration and verification. A single agent is often enough.

## Choose the Team for the Mission

- Identify independent questions or implementation slices before spawning. Keep tightly coupled changes with one owner or sequence them through task dependencies.
- Choose only the profiles and number of teammates the work needs. Research, implementation, testing, review, documentation, and other domain specialties can be combined freely.
- Treat explorer → architect → implementers, scout/builder/reviewer, and other recipes as optional examples. No role sequence is required.
- Distinguish an agent **profile** (expertise, system prompt, permissions, model preference) from Ensemble **lead/member** identity. A profile named `architect` or `orchestrator` does not grant lead privileges.
- Respect the user's delegation and model constraints. For a small or inseparable task, work directly rather than creating an unnecessary team.

## Lead Workflow

1. Define each mission's scope, deliverable, ownership boundaries, and verification criteria.
2. Create a team with `team_create` when coordination is justified.
3. Add tasks with `team_tasks_add`. Record the real returned IDs; use `depends_on` only for tasks already in this team. A dependent task must be unblocked before it can be claimed.
   When classification is enabled, wait for notifications only for tasks needing classification. Fully manual scores make a task `not_required` immediately with zero attempts and no classifier notification; observe that board state once instead of waiting for a notification that will never arrive.
4. Choose a profile, context strategy, worktree policy, and model strategy for each mission. Discover available profiles/models rather than assuming example names exist.
5. Spawn teammates one at a time, waiting for each tool result; their work runs asynchronously. Use `claim_task` for a claimable implementation task. Built-in `explore`/`plan` spawns do not auto-claim tasks.
6. Use `plan_approval: true` when a mission or project policy calls for a reviewed implementation plan. Approve/reject through `team_message`.
7. Wait for teammate messages. Use `team_results` for full content when a report is truncated or consequential; use status tools for a specific diagnostic, not a waiting loop.
8. After completion, use `team_shutdown`, then `team_merge` once the teammate is shut down. Inspect the diff and run the project's verification before `team_cleanup` and before claiming success.

## Choose Context Deliberately

On V2, choose the smallest appropriate transition:

- **`fresh`** (also the default): start an independent mission. Prefer it for an independent review or an unrelated task.
- **`fork`**: create a new teammate from useful native research/history; give it only its new identity/task delta. Set `context: { mode: "fork", from: "member-name" }` on `team_spawn`.
- **`checkpoint`**: inherit before a native `messageID`, an **exclusive** boundary. For A/B/C/D/E, choose D to keep C and omit D/E.
- **`compact_fork`**: natively compact a distinct idle source, verify completion, then fork its projected summary and retained recent context. This modifies the source's context.
- **`team_handoff({ agent })`**: change the calling session's profile for subsequent turns, keeping its identity/history/tasks/worktree. Use it for a continuation that needs another specialty, rather than an independent worker. It does not transfer leadership or create a worktree.

Only the lead spawns; any active initialized member, including the lead, may hand off itself. A teammate needing follow-up workers reports to the lead. Sources are restricted to the same team: `current` (default), `lead`, a member name, or a team session ID; a finished member is usable while its native session exists.

Read [context continuity](references/context-continuity.md) before using inheritance or handoff: it covers the same-server HTTP bridge, Git restrictions, exclusive boundaries, admission errors, and V1 compatibility. Unsupported inheritance fails explicitly; do not silently substitute fresh context or paste a synthetic conversation history.

## Profiles, Worktrees, and Models

- Built-in `explore` and `plan` are read-only profiles and skip automatic worktree creation. For a custom read-only profile, configure native edit/shell permissions and pass `worktree: false` explicitly. A name such as `reviewer` is not a permission policy.
- Writers use isolated worktrees by default. Inherited cross-directory moves require clean source/destination directories at the same Git HEAD. Integrate divergent commits before creating the inherited worktree; do not transfer files implicitly.
- Handoff preserves the directory. Turning a shared-directory researcher into a writer does not add isolation; fork an isolated worker when that is what the task needs.
- Set `model` when an explicit selection is required by the task, budget, or project. Otherwise use the configured Ensemble/native selection. A fork preserves the source's native model unless an explicit spawn model or Ensemble model-assignment setting overrides it.
- Native handoff keeps the session's selected model, independently of the target profile's default. The lead can separately use `team_message({ to, model })` to change a teammate's model.
- IDs such as `openai/gpt-5-mini` and `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` are illustrative, not required defaults. Verify available IDs and match capabilities to the mission.

## Project Integration

For interactive installation, analysis of existing agents, or changes to project configuration/instructions, use `ensemble-project-setup`. This operational skill handles team execution after setup.

Keep this skill as the reusable operating guide. In project `AGENTS.md`, add a short rule to load it when teamwork is justified, plus the project's ownership and verification policy. Use optional `.opencode/agents/*.md` files for durable expertise/permissions; put the current task and ownership boundaries in spawn prompts. Do not duplicate the entire tool protocol across every profile.

For setup, copyable `AGENTS.md` guidance, and an optional agent profile, read [project integration](references/project-integration.md). The project chooses its workflows; the plugin supplies generic coordination and continuity operations.

## Load References As Needed

- Installing or integrating into project/agent instructions: [project integration](references/project-integration.md).
- Reusing native history or changing profiles: [context continuity](references/context-continuity.md).
- Choosing an optional team shape: [coordination patterns](references/coordination-patterns.md).
- Writing a mission prompt: [prompt recipes](references/prompt-recipes.md).
- Checking spawn/merge/verification readiness: [lead checklists](references/lead-checklists.md).
- Diagnosing poor coordination: [anti-patterns](references/anti-patterns.md).
- Evaluating this skill: [eval scenarios](references/eval-scenarios.md).

## Operational Rules

- Do not invent task IDs. Use IDs returned by `team_tasks_add` when setting `depends_on` or `claim_task`.
- Keep teammate prompts short. The plugin already injects team identity, allowed tools, worktree context, and completion/blocker reporting instructions. Add the mission, not another copy of that protocol.
- Use `team_message` for reports; plain text output alone is not delivered to the lead.
- Keep spawning, shutdown, merge, and cleanup with the lead. A handoff does not bypass that authorization.
- Read the full result and inspect the integrated diff before accepting work. Report verification failures accurately.
- On V2, discover the client's Code Mode tool paths before calling them. `team_view` navigates only with `navigate: true` and an explicit user request; archived-team purge uses the existing preview/approval flow.

## Minimal Example

This is one possible bounded mission, not a required team topology. Calls below use illustrative Code Mode paths; use those exposed by your client.

```ts
await tools.team_create({ name: "cache-fix" })
await tools.team_tasks_add({ tasks: [
  { content: "Fix expired cache entries; own cache code and its focused regression tests.", priority: "high" },
] })
```

In the next call, `taskID` is the actual ID returned above:

```ts
await tools.team_spawn({
  name: "cache-worker",
  agent: "build",
  claim_task: taskID,
  prompt: "Fix expiry handling in the cache subsystem. Keep the change scoped, test expired and valid entries, run the project's focused cache checks, and report the result.",
  context: { mode: "fresh" },
})
```

If an existing member already owns relevant research, choose a native fork from that member instead. Add other missions only when they contribute independent, verifiable work.
